gamemechanicinfo-siding-text:
VS Siding Mod: Guide
A siding wall is a thin panel, a quarter of a block thick, built up in layers. Framing plus infill is a complete wall, and it seals a room the way a solid block does. Finishes are appearance only, except that one stops the light a bare wattle wall lets through.

The three layers
• plank-oak|plank-birch Framing: the timber that stands first.
• clay-blue|stick Infill: the material between the timbers.
• daubraw-browngolden|plank-oak Finish: a layer on each face.

Your first wall
1. Put a saw-copper|stone-granite saw or a stone in your off-hand slot.
2. Hold plank-oak planks in your main hand.
3. Right-click the face of the block where the wall should stand.
4. Right-click the standing frame with clay-blue clay, or with any other infill, to fill it.
5. Right-click a face with a finish to cover it. Every layer goes on the same way: right-click while the saw or stone is in your off hand.
6. Press toolmode to open the picker for corners, floors and finishes.

Contents
• Layers and materials: framing, infill and finish materials, and taking one apart.
• Floors and decks: joists, floorboards, ceilings and decks.
• Picker modes: wall, corner, diagonal, floor and face, decks, and board and log styles.
• Corners and junctions: upgrading a wall to a corner, diagonals, and where walls meet.
• Rooms, cellars and light: what seals a room, which walls cool, and what lets light through.
• Furniture and lights in walls: what the open side of a wall takes, and trunks and beds along a run.
• Starting in the stone age: building with stone, sticks and bones, no saw needed.
gamemechanicinfo-siding-walls-title: VS Siding Mod: Layers and materials
gamemechanicinfo-siding-walls-text:
VS Siding Mod: Layers and materials
A wall is built from a framing, an infill and a finish on each face.

Framing
plank-oak|plank-birch Planks, stick sticks or bone bones build the framing.

Infill
Right-click the standing frame with an infill to fill it. Infills include:
• stick Sticks, as wattle.
• drygrass Straw. It burns.
• clay-blue Clay.
• packeddirt Packed dirt.
• rammed-light-plain Rammed earth.
• hide-pelt-medium A pelt, small, medium, large or huge. It comes back as the pelt that went on. Fox, raccoon and bear pelts do not fit. It burns.
• cloth-plain Cloth. It burns.
• stone-granite Rubble stone.
• glass-plain Glass: a block, a slab or a leaded glass pane.

Finish
Right-click a filled wall with a finish to face that side. Finishes include:
• daubraw-browngolden Daub.
• plaster-plain Plaster.
• packeddirt Packed dirt.
• rammed-light-plain Rammed earth.
Right-click a face that is already finished and the finish goes on the face behind it, so a wall against the ground can be finished from inside.
A glazed wall takes a finish like any other, drawn as a border round the glass.

Taking one apart
• Breaking a wall peels one layer at a time, outermost first, on the face you hit.
• The finish goes first, then the infill, then the framing.
• The material comes back each time.

Guide, Floors and decks
gamemechanicinfo-siding-floors-title: VS Siding Mod: Floors and decks
gamemechanicinfo-siding-floors-text:
VS Siding Mod: Floors and decks
A thin floor is built in layers like a wall: joists, an infill between them, floorboards on top and a ceiling beneath. A wall carries its own, called a deck.

Laying joists
Pick Floor, then right-click the side of a block, a deck or another floor with plank-oak planks or stick sticks to lay joists in the cell beside it.

Carrying a floor on
• Right-click the top of a floor with planks to carry it on the way you are looking, up to four blocks. This is how a floor goes out over water.
• Sneak if it is filled and has no floorboards yet, or the planks become floorboards.

Filling and finishing
• Fill a floor the way you fill a wall.
• Right-click the top with a finish for floorboards.
• Right-click the underside with a finish for a ceiling.
• A finish clicked on a finished top goes on the underside, and the other way round.
• Planks on a boarded top extend the floor while Floor is picked, and go on the underside where it cannot extend, as in a cellar.

Board direction
• The Boards row sets which way the floorboards run. They default to east-west.
• daubraw-browngolden Daub on the underside shows lath strips, which follow the Boards row the same way.

Glass floors
• glass-plain Glass fills a floor too, and neighbouring glass floors merge into one pane.
• A glass floor takes floorboards and a ceiling like any other, drawn as a border round the glass.

Decks
• Deck: a floor across the top of the wall's cell, so an upper storey meets the wall with no gap.
• A new frame gets a deck as it goes up while Deck is picked.
• Right-clicking a standing wall with planks adds one.
• Right-click the deck itself to fill it and finish it like a floor.
• A wall deck takes the same layers: fill it from any side, then floorboards go on top and a ceiling underneath.
• Planks on a boarded deck go on the underside.
• Glass decks join glass floors.
• A new deck seals once it is filled.
• While Floor is picked, planks on a wall lay a floor beside it instead of facing the wall. The top or underside of a filled deck still takes them as floorboards or a ceiling.

Rugs and carpets
Rugs and carpets lie on a filled floor, and come off first when you break it.

What it seals
A filled floor seals the room below it, and its infill decides whether it cools.

Guide, Layers and materials
gamemechanicinfo-siding-modes-text:
VS Siding Mod: Picker modes
Press toolmode while a saw or a stone is in your off hand to open the picker. Its rows each keep their own choice. Click an option to pick it, and click it again to turn its row off. Framing always keeps one picked.

Framing
• Wall: a flat panel across the cell.
• Corner: an outside corner, two faces meeting. See Corners and junctions.
• Diagonal: a panel that crosses its block from corner to corner between two posts, for cutting a corner at forty-five degrees. See Corners and junctions.
• Floor: a thin floor across the top of the cell.
• Face: planks put a finish on one face of any solid block, such as the top of a log beam. Siding walls and floors take their finishes as layers, so they are left out. Boards run as the Boards row says. Right-click a face finish with planks to swap it: the same wood turns to the picked boards for free, and another wood drops the old planks.

Deck
• Deck: a floor across the top of the cell, so an upper storey meets the wall with no gap.
• A new frame gets a deck as it goes up.
• Right-clicking a standing wall with planks adds one.
• Right-click the deck itself to fill it and finish it like a floor.
• Right-clicking a standing wall with a stair instead fills its open side beside a staircase, turned to match the stair standing next to it.

Boards
For plank finishes only.
• Weatherboard: overlapping tapered boards.
• Vertical boards and Horizontal boards: plain flush boards.

Logs
For log finishes only.
• Shakes
• Logs: bare logs.
• Vertical bark
• Horizontal bark

With a row turned off, the finish takes its usual look.

Guide
gamemechanicinfo-siding-corners-title: VS Siding Mod: Corners and junctions
gamemechanicinfo-siding-corners-text:
VS Siding Mod: Corners and junctions
Where two lines of walls meet, the block they share needs a corner.

Turning a wall into a corner
• Pick Corner in the picker, then right-click the wall.
• A bare frame upgrades in place, so there is no need to break it first.
• Planks turn a filled wall into a corner when the face you click is already finished.
• On an unfinished face, planks board it instead.

Diagonals
• Diagonal crosses its block from corner to corner, between two posts.
• Diagonals placed corner to corner join into one wall.
• A diagonal takes a deck, but no step or furniture.
• On a diagonal the deck covers only the half of the block on the room side.

Where walls meet
• Where a partition meets a wall, or two walls cross, the block the two lines share takes a Corner.
• Each line of walls keeps to one side of its blocks.
• A wall lands on the far side of its block from you, so face the same way for every wall in the line.
• A wall's own block takes a deck, not a floor.
• A stair one block wide is walled from the block on each side of it.
• Where that block is also part of the floor above, the wall carries a deck.

Guide
gamemechanicinfo-siding-stoneage-title: VS Siding Mod: Starting in the stone age
gamemechanicinfo-siding-stoneage-text:
VS Siding Mod: Starting in the stone age
You can build a whole wall without a saw or any metal. Stone, sticks and bones do the work.

The stone
• Put any stone-granite stone in your off-hand slot instead of a saw.
• It works the same way, and it is never used up.
• As with anything in the off hand, hunger runs a fifth faster while it is there.

Frames
• stick Sticks build a frame, four to a frame.
• bone Bones build a frame too, two to a frame.
• A bone frame does not burn.
• Sneak and right-click to stack the next frame on top, to frame the next cell, or to carry a floor on.

Filling and finishing
• Sticks are also the wattle infill, so a right-click on a bare frame fills it with wattle.
• A hide-pelt-medium pelt or a cloth-plain cloth fills a frame too.
• daubraw-browngolden Daub over wattle makes a sealed wall with no metal.

Guide
gamemechanicinfo-siding-rooms-title: VS Siding Mod: Rooms, cellars and light
gamemechanicinfo-siding-rooms-text:
VS Siding Mod: Rooms, cellars and light
Heat retention and cellar cooling work as they would with a solid block.

Sealing a room
• Framing plus infill is a complete wall, and it seals a room the way a solid block does.
• glass-plain Glass infill seals the same way.

Cellars
The infill decides whether a wall counts as a cooling wall.
• These cool: stone-granite rubble stone, clay-blue clay, packeddirt packed dirt and rammed-light-plain rammed earth.
• These do not: stick sticks (wattle), drygrass straw, hide-pelt-medium pelts and cloth-plain cloth.

Light
• glass-plain Glass infill lets daylight straight through, and neighbouring glazed cells merge into one pane.
• Bare stick sticks (wattle) let light through until a face is finished.

Reading a wall
• Look at a wall or floor to see whether it seals.
• With a saw-copper saw or a stone-granite stone in your off hand, it lists its layers too.

Guide
gamemechanicinfo-siding-furniture-title: VS Siding Mod: Furniture and lights in walls
gamemechanicinfo-siding-furniture-text:
VS Siding Mod: Furniture and lights in walls
A wall fills only a quarter of its cell, and its open side sits empty.

Putting something in a wall
• Right-click the open side with a chest, pot, torch-basic-lit-up torch, sign or other piece of furniture.
• It takes the cell for itself.
• The wall stays put behind it and keeps sealing the room as before.
• A diagonal takes no furniture.

Changing the wall behind it
• The layers of the wall cannot be changed while something stands in front of it.
• Break the furniture first, and the wall comes back.

Trunks and beds
• A trunk or a bed laid along a straight run of wall takes both walls' cells the same way.
• A bed can also stand with its head against a wall.

Tables and other mods
• Vanilla tables share walls too.
• So do the cabinets, nightstand, coffee table and Celtic bed of Kevins Furniture, the LV and MV machines of Vintage Engineering (not the creosote oven), the cupboards and crates of Containers Bundle, and the storage of More Inventorys.
• A More Inventorys rack needs a straight run of wall at least as wide and as tall as the rack.
• A mod author can allow a block by setting vssidingHostable to true in the block's attributes.

Guide
